title: Dependency runway and contingency tiers for quarterly roadmap
creator: Avery Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a clear dependency runway (what must land when) and a set of 3 contingency tiers for roadmap features that touch multiple teams (Eng, Design, Security, Infra). The goal is to reduce surprise escalations during cycle gates and to provide automated fallbacks and communication playbooks for PMs and Eng leads.

Goals: 1) Define "runway" artifacts for each cross-team initiative: required deliverables (code, design spec, security signoff, infra readiness) and milestone dates. 2) Define 3 contingency tiers with triggers and ownership: Tier A (blocking - require redistribution of team capacity or scope cut), Tier B (partial degradation - enable feature flag with reduced UX), Tier C (non-blocking - postpone optional polish work). 3) Wire dependency metadata into the roadmap dashboard so PMs can see upstream owner, current health, and time-to-fork decision. 4) Produce a lightweight runbook with communication templates and automated Slack/channel alerts for "72h at-risk" and "24h critical" windows.

Acceptance criteria: - Roadmap dashboard shows dependency runway rows per initiative with owner and ETA. - Playbook and escalation matrix published in Confluence with examples. - Three contingency tiers documented with decision criteria and approvers. - One pilot initiative (ENG-20012 + DES-1122) uses the runway and executes a Tier B mitigation.

Approach and trade-offs: - Prefer lightweight, enforceable artifacts (date + owner + blocker flag) vs heavy gating that delays delivery. Trade-off: conservative gating reduces speed but increases predictability. We'll start with a soft rollout (visibility only) for one cycle, then require explicit gating for top-10 initiatives. - Integrations: prototype using existing roadmap dashboard (console-ops/dashboards) and link to Linear; explore automated alerts via PagerDuty for infra-critical dependencies. Trade-off: full automation increases engineering cost; staged approach recommended.

Deliverables: 1) Confluence runbook: "Dependency Runway & Contingency Tiers" 2) Roadmap dashboard column mapping and filter presets 3) Templates: Slack alert, status email, dependency owner checklist 4) Pilot retrospective note and metrics (number of escalations avoided, improved on-time delivery %)

Stakeholders: PM lead: Avery Patel; Eng leads: Priya Rao (Serving Runtime), Marcus Lee (Infra); Design lead: Lila Nguyen; Security: Omar Hassan; Ops: SRE on-call rotation.

Rollout plan: Week 0-2: Draft runbook + stakeholder sign-off. Week 3: Add runway metadata to dashboard and create filters. Week 4: Pilot on one initiative; run playbook for an induced risk scenario. Week 5: Collect feedback and adjust. Week 6: Expand to top-10 initiatives for the quarter.

Monitoring & success signals: - Reduction in unplanned cross-team escalations by 30% vs previous cycle. - 90% of top-10 initiatives have owners and ETAs in runway column by week 3. - Average time-to-decision for a 72h at-risk alert < 8 hours.

Open questions: - Should contingency tiers be enforced by gating in Linear or remain advisory? (PM/Eng sync needed) - What SLAs should Security require for signoff on new infra changes?
